t: Sum of Interaction Costs in Tree Groups II — Per-Group Edge Contribution
o: We need, summed over all same-label pairs (u,v), the tree distance dist(u,v). The classic trick: total pairwise distance equals the sum over edges of (size of one side) x (size of the other side), because every path crosses each edge at most once. Restricting to one group g: for edge e splitting the tree into sides A and B, the group-g pairs whose path crosses e contribute cnt_g(A) * cnt_g(B) = a * (total_g - a). So the answer is Σ_g Σ_e a_e(g) * (cnt_g - a_e(g)). We get each subtree's group histogram via DFS with small-to-large map merging. Example 1 (path 0-1-2, all group 1): middle edge contributes 1*2 twice -> 4. Example 4: no shared groups -> 0. With n up to 1e5, small-to-large merging keeps this near O(n log n).
k: Pairwise distance sums decompose into per-edge contributions: each path crosses an edge at most once.
For a fixed group, an edge contributes a*(cnt_g - a) where a is the count of group-g nodes in the child subtree.
Small-to-large merging of per-subtree hash maps yields near-linear total time.

a.n: Approach 1: DFS with Small-to-Large Group Histograms
a.i: Root the tree at 0. A post-order DFS returns, for each subtree, a map from group label to node count. When processing edge (child -> parent), for every group g present in the child's histogram with count a, add a * (cnt[g] - a) to the answer, since exactly those same-group pairs have their unique path crossing this edge. Merging the smaller map into the larger keeps total merge cost O(n log n).
s: Compute cnt[g] = total nodes of each group; build adjacency lists.
DFS post-order; each node returns a hash map of group->count for its subtree.
At each parent-child edge, for each (g, a) in the child's map, add a*(cnt[g]-a) to the global answer.
Merge child maps into the parent's map small-to-large; return the answer.
a.t: O(n log n) expected — each node's entry is moved O(log n) times by small-to-large merging; hash operations are O(1) average.
a.sp: O(n) — adjacency lists plus maps holding at most n entries overall along any root-to-leaf chain of merges.

a.n: Approach 2: Brute Force BFS Distances per Group
a.i: For tiny n, collect nodes by group and BFS from each node to get all-pairs distances within its group. Simple but O(n^2), only viable for very small inputs — useful as a correctness baseline for stress testing.
s: Bucket node indices by group label.
For each group, run BFS from every member and sum distances to later members.
a.t: O(n^2) — a BFS from every node within its group.

w: Lead with the edge-contribution insight; it is the intended solution and generalizes (weighted edges, counting paths through vertices). Pitfalls: 64-bit accumulation (answers reach ~n^3/8 scale), forgetting pairs are unordered (the a*(cnt-a) form handles orientation automatically), recursion depth on path-shaped trees (raise limits or iterate). Follow-ups: weighted edges multiply contributions by edge weight; vertex-based grouping asks for centroid decomposition instead.
